tasks.title: Clone, pin, and test upstream Resume-Matcher
tasks.context: Phase 0 is a research/documentation-only initiative for resume-kit. The upstream donor is Resume-Matcher at https://github.com/srbhr/Resume-Matcher, licensed Apache-2.0. Clone it into the repo-local gitignored directory ./upstream/, pin it to a single concrete commit SHA, run the upstream backend tests, and document reproducible commands and results in references/upstream-audit.md. Do not write any product code. Repo stack is Python 3.12 / uv, but upstream may have its own setup instructions; follow upstream backend test instructions as closely as possible and record any deviations or environment requirements.
acceptance_criteria: ./upstream/ exists as a clone of https://github.com/srbhr/Resume-Matcher and is checked out at a pinned full commit SHA, not a floating branch name.
references/upstream-audit.md records the exact clone command, checkout/pin command or observed SHA command, pinned full SHA, upstream license name, upstream remote URL, and current test date.

references/upstream-audit.md records the exact backend test command(s), working directory, Python/package setup used, pass/fail/error/skip counts, and notable warnings or missing environment variables.

references/upstream-audit.md summarizes upstream dependency/runtime requirements relevant to later extraction, including whether backend tests require a database, frontend build, API keys, LLM provider, browser, or PDF renderer.
references/upstream-audit.md identifies backend modules that appear runnable without upstream database/frontend coupling, based on test execution and initial inspection.
No product source files, packages, CLI, MCP, API, or tests are created or modified.
tasks.implementation_notes: Start by checking whether ./upstream/ already exists. If it exists, inspect its remote and current SHA before deciding whether to reuse it; do not delete unrelated local changes. Ensure ./upstream/ is ignored by git, but only document or minimally adjust ignore state if necessary and allowed by the existing repo conventions. Prefer upstream's documented backend test commands; if documentation is missing or broken, inspect pyproject/package files and run the narrowest backend pytest command that exercises available tests. Capture enough output in prose or fenced snippets for a reviewer to reproduce the result without committing logs. Keep references/upstream-audit.md focused on audit evidence, not future implementation design.
verification_steps: Run git -C upstream remote get-url origin and confirm it is https://github.com/srbhr/Resume-Matcher or an equivalent GitHub URL for srbhr/Resume-Matcher.
Run git -C upstream rev-parse HEAD and confirm the full SHA exactly matches the SHA recorded in references/upstream-audit.md.
Run the recorded backend test command again, or document why it cannot be rerun in the current environment, and confirm the result matches the recorded status.
Run git status --short and confirm no upstream source files are staged/tracked in the product repo.

tasks.title: Create Apache-2.0 attribution ledger
tasks.context: Phase 0 must document license and attribution obligations before any Resume-Matcher code, tests, prompts, schemas, or derived implementation are reused. Use the pinned upstream clone in ./upstream/ from task 0. Write only references/attribution.md. The deliverable must cover every subsystem intended for Reuse, Extract, or Adapt once the inventory exists, and it must also provide a clear scaffold for later extraction phases to add file-level provenance.
acceptance_criteria: references/attribution.md records the same pinned upstream full commit SHA produced by task 0 and the upstream repository URL.

references/attribution.md identifies Resume-Matcher as Apache-2.0 and summarizes concrete obligations relevant to this repo: retain notices, include applicable license text when required, mark modified files, track upstream paths and SHAs, and avoid upstream trademarks as product identity.

references/attribution.md contains a table with columns for subsystem, classification, upstream path(s), pinned SHA, reused material type, attribution requirement, modification note, and downstream target package.

The attribution table covers every Reuse, Extract, and Adapt subsystem identified in references/reuse-inventory.md if that file is available; if the inventory task is still pending, provide a clearly marked provisional table using the vision-named candidates and note it must be reconciled during final review.
references/attribution.md explicitly excludes Replace/Leave-behind subsystems from reuse attribution while still noting that they were reviewed and intentionally not reused.
No product code or non-reference documentation is modified.
tasks.implementation_notes: Read upstream LICENSE, NOTICE if present, README license references, and package metadata. Inspect candidate files only enough to determine whether they contain copyright headers or embedded third-party notices. Do not provide legal advice; write practical engineering compliance notes for later agents. Use the exact pinned SHA from task 0, not a branch. If references/reuse-inventory.md already exists from task 2, align rows with its subsystem names and classifications. If not, this task can run using the vision and initiative candidate list, with final reconciliation handled by task 3.
verification_steps: Run git -C upstream rev-parse HEAD and confirm the SHA matches references/attribution.md.
Confirm references/attribution.md includes Apache-2.0 obligations and a file/subsystem provenance table.
Cross-check at least three Reuse/Extract/Adapt attribution rows against actual upstream file paths under ./upstream/.
If references/reuse-inventory.md exists, confirm every Reuse, Extract, and Adapt row there has a corresponding attribution row.

tasks.title: Build subsystem reuse inventory and classification matrix
tasks.context: Phase 0 must classify every relevant Resume-Matcher subsystem using the Reuse / Extract / Adapt / Replace / New taxonomy. Use the pinned ./upstream/ clone from task 0 and write references/reuse-inventory.md only. This is an evidence-grounded audit: locate behavior in upstream files, inspect imports and tests, determine coupling, and classify each subsystem with a one-line justification and target package. No product code may be written.
acceptance_criteria: references/reuse-inventory.md records the same pinned full upstream commit SHA from task 0 and explains the classification taxonomy: Reuse, Extract, Adapt, Replace, New.

The inventory contains one row per relevant subsystem with at least these fields: subsystem, behavior summary, upstream path(s), commit SHA, classification, target package, key dependencies/imports, app.* coupling, upstream tests/fixtures, DB/frontend independence, no-LLM feasibility, and notes/blockers.

Every strong reusable candidate from the vision is confirmed or refuted with code-grounded reasoning: MarkItDown PDF/DOCX extraction, Pydantic schemas, LLM resume-to-JSON parsing, date restoration, job keyword extraction, tailoring prompts, diff modification model, allowed paths, blocked fields, original-value verification, skill-addition gates, malformed/unsupported change rejection, omitted-content preservation, LiteLLM support, structural evaluators, and relevant tests.

Every Adapt candidate from the vision is classified with code-grounded reasoning: LiteLLM provider integration, LLM configuration, resume parsing, job keyword extraction, improvement prompts, truthfulness prompts, skill-target planning, diff generation/verification, match scoring, cover-letter generation, and PDF/DOCX export.

Replace/Leave-behind rows cover web frontend, tracker/Kanban, SQLite persistence, TinyDB migration compatibility, API routers, settings/API-key persistence UI, application job storage, navigation/state management, frontend PDF rendering, interview-preparation UI, and full local app deployment model.

New rows cover capabilities absent from upstream: agent plugin package, MCP server, purpose-built CLI, stable public API contracts, freedom 0-10 policy, human-in-loop review controller, candidate evidence model, claim provenance, approved-claim bank, truth-validation engine as needed by resume-kit, multiple resume selection, job-hunter bridge, deterministic ATS engine, and standalone no-LLM analysis mode.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use rg under ./upstream/ to find candidate modules, tests, prompts, config, API routers, persistence, and frontend boundaries. Favor upstream package metadata and imports over guesswork. When a subsystem spans multiple files, list the important files and summarize dependencies rather than pasting long code. Classifications should be conservative: Reuse only for mostly unchanged behavior, Extract for behavior that can be moved with minimal changes, Adapt for useful behavior needing new APIs/boundaries, Replace for unsuitable upstream implementation, and New where there is no meaningful equivalent. Keep target package names aligned with the initiative: document-parser, schemas, llm, matching, alignment, policy, export, tests/characterization, tests/fixtures, mcp, cli, api, evidence, ats, integrations/job-hunter.
verification_steps: Run git -C upstream rev-parse HEAD and confirm the SHA matches every inventory row or the inventory-level SHA policy.
Use rg to spot-check at least one upstream source path and one upstream test path for parsing, matching, diff/alignment, provider/config, and export subsystems.
Confirm each vision-named Strong/Adapt/Replace/New candidate appears in references/reuse-inventory.md exactly once or is intentionally grouped with an explicit note.
Confirm every row answers whether it can run without upstream DB/frontend and whether it can operate without an LLM.

tasks.title: Reconcile Phase 0 deliverables and document reviewer spot-check
tasks.context: This final Phase 0 task verifies that the three documentation deliverables are internally consistent, reproducible, and complete against initiative exit criteria. It depends on the upstream audit, attribution ledger, and reuse inventory. It may edit all three reference docs to fix inconsistencies, add missing cross-links, and record the orchestrator/reviewer spot-check evidence. Do not write product code.
acceptance_criteria: references/upstream-audit.md, references/reuse-inventory.md, and references/attribution.md all record the same pinned full upstream commit SHA and upstream repository URL.
references/upstream-audit.md contains reproducible clone and backend test instructions with captured test results.
references/reuse-inventory.md classifies every relevant subsystem and every vision-named reuse/adapt/replace/new candidate.
references/attribution.md covers every subsystem classified Reuse, Extract, or Adapt in references/reuse-inventory.md.

At least three inventory rows are spot-checked against actual upstream files and tests, and the spot-check results are recorded in references/upstream-audit.md or a clearly marked review section in the relevant reference docs.
The final docs clearly state Phase 0 wrote no product code and that ./upstream/ is a gitignored reference clone, not distributed product code.
tasks.implementation_notes: Perform consistency checks after tasks 0-2 complete. Reconcile naming differences between inventory and attribution instead of duplicating near-identical subsystem names. Spot-check rows should include varied risk areas, for example one deterministic parser/schema row, one diff/alignment policy row, and one replace/leave-behind web/persistence row. Keep edits limited to references/upstream-audit.md, references/reuse-inventory.md, and references/attribution.md. Do not transition the initiative phase; the orchestrator owns Metis phase changes.
verification_steps: Run git -C upstream rev-parse HEAD and compare it against all three reference docs.
Run rg for the pinned SHA across references/upstream-audit.md references/reuse-inventory.md references/attribution.md and confirm all three include it.
Run rg for each classification label in references/reuse-inventory.md and confirm Reuse, Extract, Adapt, Replace, and New are represented where applicable.
Manually compare every Reuse/Extract/Adapt row in references/reuse-inventory.md with references/attribution.md and confirm attribution coverage.
Run git status --short and confirm only ./upstream/ plus the three reference docs are affected by Phase 0 work, with no product code changes.
